title: Playing with text
description:
Write three string functions:

```python
def initials(name): ...          # first letters of the first and last words: "ada lovelace" -> "A.L."; "Grace Brewster Hopper" -> "G.H."
def is_palindrome(text): ...     # reads the same backwards, ignoring case and spaces
def count_vowels(text): ...      # how many of a, e, i, o, u (either case)
```

Names may have extra spaces between or around the words; an empty name gives `""`.
hints:
Each `def` is a small function: it receives values in its brackets and hands a result back with `return`. A `return` inside an `if` ends the function there. Lesson 3.01 covers functions in full.

```python
def shout(text):
    if text == "":
        return "(nothing)"
    return text.upper() + "!"
```

`name.split()` with no argument splits on any run of whitespace and ignores spaces at the ends. It gives a list of the words, which you index just like a string: `words[0]` is the first word, `words[-1]` the last, and `words[0][0]` the first letter of the first word. An empty name gives an empty list, which is falsy.
For the palindrome, first build a lower-case copy without spaces (`replace(" ", "")`), then compare it with its reverse `s[::-1]`.
`count` counts one vowel at a time; add up the five counts.
